title: Chào buổi sáng
summary: A warm morning greeting for starts, check-ins, cafes, and tours.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Chào buổi sáng is useful when the day is just starting and you want the greeting to feel warmer than a plain hello. It fits hotel breakfasts, cafes, morning tours, classes, and front-desk moments.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Use it as a friendly good morning when the setting has enough space for a greeting before the practical request.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: The phrase keeps the greeting first, then names the morning.

sections.title: Natural variations
sections.body: Switch to these when the time or relationship matters more than the morning itself.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use it before a morning order, when meeting a guide early, at breakfast, or when greeting hotel staff before asking a question.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Time-of-day greetings are pleasant but optional. If you are rushing or unsure, Xin chào is still the most dependable greeting.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: Morning greetings often lead into these practical phrases.
